scenario: A customer-facing agent that installs into multiple Slack workspaces using a developer-owned OAuth app
verdict: Straightforward to test; commercial launch has a substantial review and product-eligibility gate.
firstDecision: Check Marketplace eligibility before investing in a broad off-platform agent: an MCP-only app without meaningful Slack functionality is unsuitable under current guidelines.

testVsProduction.test: Create in a development workspace, configure scopes, and install there. Enable public distribution plus an OAuth handler for an early-customer pilot.
testVsProduction.production: Commercial distribution belongs in the Slack Marketplace. Do not treat unlisted distribution or customer-created templated apps as a general commercial workaround.
testVsProduction.caveat: The FAQ still describes unlisted apps as installable via a shared URL; newer distribution and policy documentation adds commercial restrictions. Installation capability does not establish commercial eligibility.

activeSetup.basis: Planning estimate for configuration and a first install, assuming a workspace and working HTTPS OAuth callback; not measured or promised by Slack.

productionPreparation.basis: Planning estimate for onboarding, least-privilege justification, policies, QA, and review materials; depends strongly on existing product maturity.

providerWait.value: Up to 10 business days preliminary review, then up to 10 weeks functional review for new submissions
providerWait.basis: Provider-published estimates, not guarantees. The app settings submission page can show a more current queue estimate.

timing.unboundedDependency: Reaching and retaining 10 active-workspace installs can dominate the schedule before submission. No reliable total launch date can be promised.

requirements.text: A Slack workspace where you can create and install the app; customer admins can impose separate installation restrictions.
An HTTPS OAuth callback; minimum bot scopes; client ID and client secret held server-side. Validate state and protect tokens.
For Marketplace: a working, externally installable product, tested installation/onboarding/uninstallation, support and policy links, scope justification, and review access with dummy data.
Keep at least 10 active-workspace installations throughout review. Current guidelines also mention 10 weekly active users; confirm both before submitting.

steps.title: Check product eligibility
steps.detail: Compare the intended agent experience with Marketplace suitability rules before selecting scopes. If the experience is only an external MCP server, redesign the Slack-facing functionality or ask Slack for clarification.

steps.title: Create the development app
steps.detail: Sign in, choose Create an app / Blank app, give it a name, and choose the development workspace. UI labels are documented rather than tested behind login.

steps.title: Configure least-privilege OAuth
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions add the HTTPS redirect URL and only scopes needed by implemented actions. Prefer bot scopes; request user scopes only for a specific user-acting requirement. Keep Sign in with Slack scopes in a separate flow.

steps.title: Wire the callback and test one workspace
steps.detail: Send customers to /oauth/v2/authorize; validate state in the callback and exchange the code using oauth.v2.access server-side. Use the same redirect_uri in authorization and exchange when supplied. Install, exercise an intended action, then uninstall.

steps.title: Run an external pilot
steps.detail: Complete Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces checklist and activate public distribution. Test a fresh customer's install. Gather the required active installations; customer admin approval remains a separate dependency.

steps.title: Prepare and submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Use Submit to the Slack Marketplace, provide listing details, scope rationale, a working install path, and dummy-data test access. Address automated findings and reviewer feedback. Record the dashboard's current queue estimate.

blockers.trigger: Only an external MCP server or no meaningful in-Slack functionality
blockers.nextAction: Revisit product eligibility before promising commercial launch. Contact Slack with a concrete UX description if interpretation is unclear.

blockers.trigger: History ingestion is too slow in an unlisted pilot
blockers.nextAction: New commercial unlisted apps and new installations can receive only one conversations.history/replies request per minute with 15 results. Design the pilot accordingly and pursue Marketplace review; internal customer-built apps are treated differently.
Have the customer request workspace admin approval. Provider Marketplace review does not replace customer workspace approval.

Check the special rules: paid Slack workspaces only, enforced with team.billing:read and revocation when needed; user-history/file collection has restrictions. This is a use-case rule, not a universal prerequisite for every Slack app.
Match the configured redirect URL and authorization/exchange redirect_uri; request only implemented scopes and reinstall when permissions change.

agentCanDo: Research current official rules and flag contradictions
Draft a minimal manifest, scope mapping, OAuth callback, and review checklist
Implement token storage and installation handling in the developer's backend
Prepare QA scripts and draft scope justifications or a review demo outline
humanMustDo: Sign in, choose the owning workspace, and authorize installs
Handle client secrets through a secret manager
Approve policy statements and submit the provider review
Recruit pilot workspaces and answer provider feedback
